skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Generate and edit AI videos through the inference.sh belt CLI using text, images, references, audio, and existing video.
skill.summary: Create AI video workflows across generation, animation, lipsync, editing, upscaling, sound, and merging models.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: The Ruby backtick alerts are Markdown formatting false positives, while one remote image reference can trigger a low-risk external request. Semantic review found broad belt command authorization and undisclosed third-party processing of user media. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The Bash allowlist grants all belt subcommands.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict authorization to the required belt subcommands where supported, and require confirmation for login or other account-changing operations.

remediation.issue: Media examples send user assets to external inference providers without a privacy warning.
remediation.suggestion: State that inputs are processed externally and require users to confirm rights, consent, sensitivity, and provider policies before submission.

remediation.issue: The skill embeds an externally hosted image that may load during rendering.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the image with the skill or use a marketplace-hosted asset to avoid unintended third-party requests.

content.value_statement: Choosing and operating video generation models requires many separate workflows. This skill provides direct belt CLI guidance for generation, animation, editing, audio, and finishing tasks.
actual_capabilities: Selects documented models for text-to-video and image-to-video tasks.
Runs reference-based character animation with supported Seedance and HappyHorse models.
Creates talking-head and lipsync videos from portrait and audio inputs.
Edits existing video through natural-language instructions.
Upscales video, generates foley audio, and merges clips with documented utility apps.
Browses available video applications through the belt CLI catalog.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI, an authenticated account, and network access.
Media inputs must be available through URLs accepted by the selected provider.
Supported parameters, duration, resolution, quality, and audio features vary by model.
The skill does not verify media rights, subject consent, provider policies, or output accuracy.

use_cases.title: Produce Social Video Concepts
use_cases.description: Generate short visual concepts from campaign copy, then compare fast and high-quality model options.

use_cases.title: Animate Product Artwork
use_cases.description: Turn approved product images into motion clips and add controlled camera movement or environmental effects.

use_cases.title: Build Training Presenters
use_cases.description: Create consented talking-head clips from a portrait and recorded narration, then upscale the final video.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a short video of [subject] performing [action] in [setting]. Choose a fast text-to-video model and ask before running the command.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a basic text prompt and a fast model.

prompt_templates.title: Animate an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate the image at [image URL]. Add [motion], preserve the main subject, and recommend a suitable image-to-video model before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add motion to a user-provided image.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Consented Presenter
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a talking-head video from [portrait URL] and [audio URL]. Confirm subject consent, explain external processing, then select a supported avatar model.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce a narrated avatar clip with privacy checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Finished Video Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pipeline for [goal] using generation, editing, foley, upscaling, and merging. Compare model tradeoffs and request approval before each external run.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate multiple models and utilities for a production workflow.

output_examples.input: Create a five-second sunset beach clip with realistic waves.
output_examples.output: Recommended model: Grok Imagine Video. Planned result: a five-second cinematic beach scene with waves, warm sunset light, and stable camera motion.

output_examples.input: Animate a product photograph with a slow camera orbit.
output: Motion direction: slow orbit, stable product geometry, restrained background movement.
Execution waits for the image URL and user approval.

output_examples.input: Finish a silent clip for a product announcement.
output: Generate matching foley from the approved clip.
Merge additional clips with a fade transition after reviewing each result.

best_practices: Confirm the selected model, expected duration, resolution, and audio behavior before execution.
Use media only when rights and subject consent are clear, and disclose external processing.
Test a short, economical generation before requesting longer or higher-quality output.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private portraits, recordings, or videos without informed consent and provider review.
Do not assume every model accepts the same fields, durations, resolutions, or reference formats.
Do not run installation, login, or paid generation commands without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the belt CLI, an authenticated inference.sh account, network access, and valid inputs for the selected model.

faq.question: Can it create video from text?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents text-to-video workflows for Veo, Grok, Seedance, HappyHorse, P-Video, and WAN models.

faq.question: Can it animate an image?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports documented image-to-video workflows and reference-based generation with several providers.

faq.question: Does it support sound?
faq.answer: Some generation models can create synchronized audio. The skill also documents a separate foley application for existing video.

faq.question: Can it edit and upscale video?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents natural-language video editing and a Topaz upscaling application.

faq.question: Are media inputs processed locally?
faq.answer: No. Belt sends requests to external inference services, so users should review privacy, consent, rights, and provider terms first.
